title: Spinning giant optomechanical cavity with nonreciprocal self-interference
abstract: We study a spinning optomechanical cavity that is coupled to a meandering waveguide at multiple spatially separated points, forming a giant-cavity configuration. The resulting self-interference makes the effective optical driving, linewidth, and frequency shift strongly dependent on the propagation phase in the waveguide, while the rotation-induced Sagnac-Fizeau shift causes the clockwise (CW) and counterclockwise (CCW) cavity modes to experience distinct interference phases. Under single-tone driving, this mechanism enables phase-controlled phonon cooling and, in the presence of cavity rotation, nonreciprocal cooling, with one propagation direction approaching the mechanical ground-state regime while the opposite direction remains less efficiently cooled. Under two-tone driving, the same interference mechanism engineers a squeezed reservoir for the mechanical mode, producing steady-state squeezing that likewise becomes nonreciprocal under cavity rotation. These results establish multi-point self-interference as a versatile mechanism for phase-controlled optomechanical reservoir engineering and show that, when combined with cavity rotation, it provides a route to nonreciprocal quantum effects.
summary: This paper investigates how multi-point self-interference in a spinning optomechanical cavity allows for precise, phase-controlled engineering of the mechanical quantum reservoir. By combining this interference effect with cavity rotation, the authors demonstrate a novel route to achieving nonreciprocal quantum phenomena, such as directional phonon cooling and squeezing.
main_problem: The study aims to engineer quantum mechanical reservoirs with precise phase control and nonreciprocal behavior by combining cavity rotation with multi-point self-interference.
main_result: The mechanism successfully enables phase-controlled phonon cooling and generates nonreciprocal steady-state squeezing for the mechanical mode when cavity rotation is introduced.
method: The analysis uses the input-output formalism and quantum Langevin equations to model the coupled optomechanical system under single-tone (cooling) and two-tone (squeezing) driving.
model_or_system: The system is a spinning optomechanical cavity coupled to a meandering waveguide at multiple points, forming a giant-cavity structure. The dynamics are governed by the interplay between cavity rotation (Sagnac-Fizeau shift) and phase-dependent self-interference.
key_observables: Effective linewidth ($\kappa_{	ext{eff}}$), effective detuning ($\Delta_{	ext{eff}}$), steady-state phonon number ($ ar{n}$), and squeezing level ($S$).
important_parameters: Cavity rotation rate ($\Omega$), propagation phase ($\phi_j$), driving tones (single/two-tone), and coupling strength ($g$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Markovian approximation for the mechanical bath noise and often uses the center-phase approximation for frequency-dependent calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup (Fig. 1) and compare contours of squeezing levels derived from center-phase vs. frequency-dependent calculations, and RWA vs. time-periodic calculations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical setup and the origin of nonreciprocity via self-interference, to deriving the necessary equations for cooling and squeezing, and finally analyzing the results for both single-tone and two-tone driving regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a sophisticated theoretical blueprint for controlling quantum dissipation and generating nonreciprocal quantum effects in solid-state optomechanical systems, which is highly relevant to quantum sensing and quantum transduction.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of a giant spinning optomechanical cavity. A spinning ring cavity is evanescently coupled to a meander- ing waveguide at multiple spatially separated points, forming a giant-cavity configuration. The cavity supports two coun- terpropagating optical modes, denoted by CW and CCW, whose resonance frequencies are shifted in opposite directions by the rotation at angular velocity Ω. The multi-point waveg- uide coupling leads to self-interference, which makes the effec- tive detuning, dissipation, and driving phase dependent and direction dependent.

FIG. 2. Phase dependence of the effective optical linewidth κj/ωm (solid) and detuning ∆j/ωm (dashed) for N = 4 in the overcoupled limit κ0 ≃0. Multi-point self-interference strongly modulates the linewidth, allowing the system to be tuned between the resolved- and unresolved-sideband regimes. The parameters are κex,j ≃38 MHz and ωm ≃85 MHz.

FIG. 3. Phase-dependent cooling for a static cavity. (a) Logarithm of the steady-state phonon number, log10(¯nj), and (b) effective linewidth, κj/ωm, as functions of the driving de- tuning δd and the reference phase ϕj,0. The yellow dashed contour in (a) and dashed line in (b) mark the ¯nj = 1 thresh- old and the boundary κj = ωm between the resolved- and unresolved-sideband regimes, respectively. The parameters are κex,j ≃38 MHz, ωm ≃85 MHz, γm ≃3 kHz, T ≃3 K, g ≃67 Hz, P ≃5.4 W, L ≃4×10−3 m, and vg ≃1.1×107 m/s.

FIG. 4. Nonreciprocal phonon cooling for the two opposite driving directions. (a) Logarithm of the steady-state phonon number, log10(¯nj), as a function of the driving detuning δd at T ≃3 K. (b) log10(¯nj) as a function of the temperature T at the reference red-sideband point δd ≃0. The reference phases are chosen as ϕcw,0 ≃0.34π and ϕccw,0 ≃0.38π, correspond- ing to a phase difference δϕ0 ≃0.04π between the two coun- terpropagating modes. For the spinning cavity considered here, we take |∆F | = 2.08ωm, corresponding to Ω≈30 kHz. The other parameters are the same as those in Fig. 3.

FIG. 5. Phase-dependent mechanical squeezing for a static cavity. (a) Optimized mechanical squeezing Sj and (b) the corresponding optimal two-tone coupling ratio Gj,+/Gj,−as functions of the driving detuning δd and the reference phase ϕj,0. The red solid and dashed contours in (a) indicate Sj = 0 dB and Sj = 3 dB, respectively. Only stable parameter points satisfying Eq. (48) and Gj,+ < Gj,−are retained. The red-tone input power is P−≃3.4 W, the mechanical damping rate is γm ≃2 kHz, and the temperature is T ≃0.1 K. The other parameters are the same as those in Fig. 3.
